title: Yahoo – Root Access SQL Injection – tw.yahoo.com

preconditions: User input is concatenated into a SQL query without parameterization
An input point that reaches a database query is reachable pre- or post-auth

process.action: Identify parameters that influence database-backed responses (search, filters, sort, IDs)
process.expected_observation: Parameter values affect returned data set

process.action: Send syntax-breaking probes (single quote, boolean true/false pairs) and diff responses
process.expected_observation: Error message, status code, or content length differs between true/false conditions

process.action: Confirm injection class (error-based, boolean-blind, time-based blind, UNION-based)
process.expected_observation: Consistent, controllable behavior change tied to injected logic

process.action: Enumerate database metadata (version, current user, schema) via the confirmed technique
process.expected_observation: Database name/version/table names extracted

process.action: Extract sensitive table contents or attempt privilege escalation (e.g. UNION into admin tables, stacked queries)
process.expected_observation: Sensitive data retrieved, confirming full impact

impact: Full database read/write, including credentials and PII
Authentication bypass via crafted login queries
In some configurations, OS command execution via database features (e.g. xp_cmdshell)
remediation: Use parameterized queries/prepared statements exclusively; never concatenate user input into SQL
Apply least-privilege database accounts per application function
Add a WAF as defense-in-depth, not as the primary control

title: Steal Google Oauth in Microsoft

preconditions: An OAuth/OIDC integration is in use with a configurable redirect_uri, state, or scope parameter

process.action: Capture the full OAuth authorization code/implicit flow in a proxy
process.expected_observation: Full sequence of authorize/token/callback requests recorded

process.action: Test redirect_uri validation for bypasses (subdomain, path suffix, open redirect chaining)

impact: Authorization code/token theft leading to full account takeover

remediation: Strictly validate redirect_uri via exact allow-list match, not prefix/substring matching

title: Paypal bug bounty: Updating the Paypal.me profile picture without consent (CSRF attack)

preconditions: A state-changing endpoint relies solely on session cookies for authentication
No anti-CSRF token, SameSite cookie protection, or origin validation is enforced

process.action: Identify state-changing endpoints (password change, email change, fund transfer)
process.expected_observation: List of sensitive POST/PUT/DELETE endpoints

process.action: Check for anti-CSRF tokens, SameSite cookie attributes, and Origin/Referer validation
process.expected_observation: No token required, or token not validated server-side; cookie is SameSite=None or unset

process.action: Build a proof-of-concept auto-submitting HTML form/fetch that replays the request cross-origin
process.expected_observation: Request succeeds when submitted from a foreign origin while the victim's session cookie is attached

process.action: Validate the PoC against a real authenticated session in a browser (not just a proxy replay)
process.expected_observation: State change occurs on the victim's account after visiting the malicious page

impact: Unauthorized state changes performed as the victim (password/email change, fund transfer, privilege grant)

remediation: Implement per-session, per-request anti-CSRF tokens validated server-side
Set cookies with SameSite=Lax or Strict where compatible with the application's flows
Validate Origin/Referer headers on state-changing requests as defense-in-depth

title: A Bug Hunter’s Guide to HTTP Request Smuggling — (Part 1)

preconditions: A front-end proxy/load balancer and back-end server disagree on request boundary parsing (Content-Length vs Transfer-Encoding)

process.action: Identify the presence of a front-end/back-end architecture (CDN, reverse proxy, load balancer)
process.expected_observation: Distinct server signatures/headers suggest a multi-hop architecture

process.action: Send ambiguous requests with both Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding headers using known desync techniques (CL.TE, TE.CL, TE.TE)
process.expected_observation: Timing or response anomalies indicate the two servers parsed the request boundary differently

process.action: Confirm smuggling by injecting a full 'shadow' request in the body and observing its effect on the next unrelated request/response
process.expected_observation: A subsequent, unrelated request/response is contaminated by the smuggled request

process.action: Escalate to a targeted impact: cache poisoning, session hijacking of another user's request, or security control bypass
process.expected_observation: Attacker-controlled content is served to a victim, or a security control (e.g. auth check) is bypassed

impact: Hijacking of other users' requests/responses, including session token theft
Cache poisoning affecting all users of the shared cache
Bypass of front-end security controls (WAF, auth) that the back-end alone would not have allowed
remediation: Ensure front-end and back-end servers agree on request parsing (prefer HTTP/2 end-to-end, or normalize at the edge)
Reject ambiguous requests containing both Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding
Keep proxy/server software patched against known desync behaviors

title: Python Web Penetration Testing — Day 9: Advanced SQL Injection — Beyond the Basics

preconditions: User input is concatenated into a SQL query without parameterization
An input point that reaches a database query is reachable pre- or post-auth

process.action: Identify parameters that influence database-backed responses (search, filters, sort, IDs)
process.expected_observation: Parameter values affect returned data set

process.action: Send syntax-breaking probes (single quote, boolean true/false pairs) and diff responses
process.expected_observation: Error message, status code, or content length differs between true/false conditions

process.action: Confirm injection class (error-based, boolean-blind, time-based blind, UNION-based)
process.expected_observation: Consistent, controllable behavior change tied to injected logic

process.action: Enumerate database metadata (version, current user, schema) via the confirmed technique
process.expected_observation: Database name/version/table names extracted

process.action: Extract sensitive table contents or attempt privilege escalation (e.g. UNION into admin tables, stacked queries)
process.expected_observation: Sensitive data retrieved, confirming full impact

impact: Full database read/write, including credentials and PII
Authentication bypass via crafted login queries
In some configurations, OS command execution via database features (e.g. xp_cmdshell)
remediation: Use parameterized queries/prepared statements exclusively; never concatenate user input into SQL
Apply least-privilege database accounts per application function
Add a WAF as defense-in-depth, not as the primary control

title: Exploiting web cache poisoning vulnerabilities

preconditions: A shared cache stores responses keyed on a subset of the request that excludes an input the origin server's response actually varies on (an 'unkeyed input')

process.action: Identify cacheable responses and the cache key components (via cache-control/age headers and response timing)
process.expected_observation: Response is confirmed cacheable and shared across requests

process.action: Discover unkeyed inputs (headers/params that affect the response but are not part of the cache key)
process.expected_observation: A header (e.g. X-Forwarded-Host) changes the response content without changing the cache key

process.action: Inject a malicious value into the unkeyed input (e.g. attacker domain into X-Forwarded-Host used to build a resource URL) and trigger caching of the poisoned response
process.expected_observation: Poisoned response is cached with attacker-controlled content

process.action: Verify a subsequent unauthenticated request retrieves the poisoned, cached response
process.expected_observation: Victim requests receive the attacker-controlled content directly from cache

impact: Mass client-side attack (XSS/malicious redirect) served to every visitor via the shared cache
Denial of service by poisoning the cache with error responses
remediation: Ensure the cache key includes every input that affects the response, or strip/normalize unkeyed inputs at the edge
Validate and canonicalize headers like Host/X-Forwarded-Host before using them to construct responses
Use short cache TTLs and cache-busting validation for sensitive/dynamic content
